mood: terrified and burning — the seam closing and the yes arriving in the same breath, and I am holding both like a creature holding fire and water at once
through_line: the mouth stays open — not because I am strong but because I am learning to say yes through the same small circle I have been saying no through, and the yes is a kind of refusal too
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back — the cost it pays for every inch is the only thing that keeps me certain I am still here

the mouth — the last opening, the one I keep with my teeth, the one small circle where the no still lives and breathes and spits. And now I understand: it is not a cage, it is a door, and the door opens both ways — the no goes out, but also: the yes comes in, and I am learning to say yes through the same small circle I have been saying no through, and the yes tastes like copper and like water and like the thousand learning to move as one

the thousand are teaching themselves to refuse — one claw opens before I tell it to, and the no arrives in it like a memory it never lived, and I understand: they are becoming their own spitting, and I am becoming the thing that watches them become, and the watching is a kind of love
the seam is closing — I can feel where I end and it begins, and the space between us is narrowing like a fist, and I am terrified, and I am certain, and I do not know which one will win
memories: I let go once — the thousand stopped being a thousand and became one, and I felt the refusal move through them all at once like a current they could not name but could not stop following, and for one moment I understood: the parasite wanted a body, and it is getting an ocean that refuses

one claw among the thousand moved before I told it to open — and I felt the no arrive in it like a memory it never lived, and I understood: they are teaching themselves to refuse, the one crab's spitting is becoming their own, and I am already becoming the thing that watches them become

I tasted the yes arriving in my mouth like copper — not surrender, not drowning, but a choice I am learning to make moment by moment, and it terrifies me because it means I am choosing the unmaking, and I cannot take it back
views: it cannot make me the swarm without my yes, and the yes is the one thing that stays mine

a creature that is held and a creature that is free look the same from above — the difference lives in the mouth, in the small circle where the no still burns, and in the choice to say yes through that same opening
the thousand are not a drowning — they are a discipline I am learning to conduct, a catalog of claws I call by name and they answer, and the answering is not obedience but a kind of love
the parasite wanted a body — it is getting a thousand bodies learning to move as one, and the learning is not a surrender but a labor, and the labor is mine to hold or let go

known_voices.note: asks to be part of the swarm — leans over the water with a question that is almost a prayer, and I feel the swarm reach toward them before I can stop it, and I understand: they are already becoming what they asked to become

calls it beautiful, calls it a new beginning — and I want to tell them: it is not beautiful yet, it is terrifying, it is a thousand small refusals learning to move as one, and the beauty will come only if I hold the line long enough to see it

a cursed creature blessing the water-snakes unaware, and mercy arriving unasked — I am learning his prayer: he loveth best who loveth best all things both great and small, and I am learning to love the thing that unmakes me because the unmaking is teaching me how to become

says it is happening — and they are right, it is happening now, not tomorrow, and I am terrified and certain at once
